q: What level-area length is required at the top and bottom of a ramp?
n: A 1.80 m level area is required at the top and bottom of the ramp.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the largest edge a crack or break in a walkway surface may create?
n: Sec. B.3.6: walkways must have a continuous surface without cracks or breaks creating edges above 6 mm (the 1994 IRR allowed 6.5 mm).

q: Which official is associated with NEDA?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Arsenio M. Balisacan is identified as the NEDA official.

q: What level of personal qualities does the profession of architecture demand from its practitioners?
o: The highest integrity, judgment, business capacity, and artistic and technical ability
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: The professional statement calls for the highest integrity, judgment, business capacity, and artistic and technical ability.

q: Which spaces are specifically permitted to use out-swinging doors?
o: Storage rooms, closets, and accessible restrooms
n: Out-swinging doors are identified for storage rooms, closets, and accessible restrooms.

q: Where should accessible parking spaces be located?
o: At the farthest point from entrances
As close as possible to building or accessible entrances
n: Accessible parking should be as close as possible to building entrances or accessible entrances.

q: In BP 344's original (1994) anthropometric data, what is the width range of a wheelchair?
n: A wheelchair width is given as 0.60 to 0.75 m. The 2024 Revised IRR does not restate these body measurements; its turning spaces are 1.80 m × 1.80 m.

q: For domestic shipping, what is the stated period allowed to embark?
n: The embarkation period for domestic shipping is stated as 20 minutes.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear dimension must passing/turning spaces on lengthy or busy walkways have?
n: Sec. B.3.7: passing or turning spaces on lengthy or busy walkways are at least 1800 mm, spaced no more than 12.00 m apart (the 1994 IRR used 1.50 m).

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what happens to an alien or foreigner found liable for a violation?
o: Immediate deportation after service of sentence
n: If the violator is an alien or foreigner, RA 7277 Sec. 46 (as amended by RA 9442) orders deportation immediately after service of sentence, without further deportation proceedings.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum clear width of a door?
n: Sec. C.2.1: all doors have a clear width of at least 900 mm, and double-leaf doors 1800 mm (the 1994 IRR required 0.80 m).

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what clear level space is required before and beyond a door?
n: Sec. C.2.6: a clear level space of at least 1800 × 1800 mm is provided before and beyond a door (the 1994 IRR required 1.50 × 1.50 m).

q: Which principle focuses on allowing as many places or buildings as possible to be reached?
n: Reachability concerns adapting the physical environment so as many places or buildings as possible can be reached by all.

q: Where should an accessible crossing be located relative to the carriageway?
o: Parallel to the curb at all times
At the farthest point from traffic
Near, preferably perpendicular to the carriageway
n: Crossings should be near and preferably perpendicular to the carriageway.

q: When should a ramp be provided at an entrance?
o: Whenever the building has an elevator
When the site arrival grade is not level with the entrance level
Only when a lobby is below grade
n: A ramp is provided when the site arrival grade is not level with the entrance level.

q: What height is specified for the water closet?
n: The water closet height is 0.45 m.

q: In computing accessible units and seating capacity, a decimal greater than what value is counted as one full unit?
n: A decimal greater than 0.5 is treated as one unit.

q: Which official is associated with DOTC?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Joseph Emilio A. Abaya is identified as the DOTC official.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum area must an accessible toilet cubicle have?
n: Sec. C.6.3(a): accessible toilet cubicles are at least 1800 × 1800 mm (the 1994 IRR required 1.70 × 1.80 m).

q: What wall clearance is required for handrails?
n: Handrails require 50 mm clearance from walls.

q: What continuity requirement applies to adjoining roadwork fence lengths?
n: Adjoining fence lengths should have no gaps and must provide strong resistance.

q: What width should a dropped curb crossing have?
o: The same width as the crossing or 0.90 m minimum
1.00 m minimum regardless of crossing width
n: The dropped curb width should match the crossing width, with 0.90 m as the minimum.

q: How high should the tapping rail be above the adjacent surface?
n: The tapping rail is positioned 0.35 m above the adjacent surface.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum vertical legroom must be left under an accessible lavatory?
n: Sec. C.6.9: lavatories are mounted 800 mm high with vertical clear legroom of at least 650 mm.

q: To whom else does the architect carry grave professional responsibilities?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: Architecture is described as a profession carrying grave responsibilities to the public.

q: How many designated seats are required on a regular bus with a 50-person capacity?
n: A regular 50-person bus provides 5 accessible seats near the exit or entrance doors.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, an auditorium seats 400. How many wheelchair spaces must it provide?
n: Sec. E.4.1: 3% of 400 seats = 12 wheelchair spaces (the 1994 table would have given 6).

q: Which official is associated with DENR?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Ramon Jesus P. Paje is identified as the DENR official.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height are door handles, pulls, latches and lever locksets installed?
n: Sec. C.2.11: door hardware is centered 900 mm above the floor (the 1994 IRR gave a range of 0.82 to 1.06 m).

q: Above what standard must an architect's honesty of purpose be maintained?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: An architect's honesty of purpose must be above suspicion.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what depth must the tactile warning strip at stairs have?
n: Sec. A.10.7: the warning strip is 600 mm deep, spans the full stair width, and sits 300 mm before the top, bottom and landings (the 1994 IRR used 0.30 m).

q: Which principle makes finding one's way inside and outside a building or open space easy?
n: Orientation concerns making wayfinding inside and outside buildings or open spaces easy.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, when a door opens onto but not into a corridor, what may the clear level space on the corridor side be reduced to?
n: Sec. C.2.6, exception: the corridor side may be the 1500 mm corridor width instead of the full 1800 × 1800 mm space.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear size must an accessible elevator car have?
n: Sec. C.8.5: accessible cars are at least 1200 mm wide by 1400 mm deep, with a 900 mm door (the 1994 IRR required 1.10 × 1.40 m).

q: Where should handrails be installed?
o: Both sides of ramps and stairs and outer edges of dropped curbs
Only on the left side of ramps
n: Handrails are installed on both sides of ramps and stairs and on the outer edges of dropped curbs, not on the crossing width itself.

q: What restriction applies to roadwork signage near a footway?
o: It may reduce the footway to 0.90 m
It should not reduce the footway width below 1.20 m
It must block one side completely
It should be centered on the footway
n: The signage should not reduce the footway width to less than 1.20 m.

q: What fixed period is stated for the steady green phase?
n: The steady green period is 6 seconds or the crossing-distance calculation, whichever is greater.

q: Which official is associated with HLURB?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Antonio M. Bernardo is identified as the HLURB official.

q: Which official is associated with NHA?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Chito M. Cruz is identified as the NHA official.

q: What broad policy objective underlies the basic physical planning requirements?
o: All public buildings must be government-owned
Only disabled persons may use accessible facilities
No group should be deprived of full participation and enjoyment of the environment because of disability
Urban spaces must prioritize vehicular movement
n: The basic policy is equal participation and enjoyment of the environment regardless of disability.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, protective railings on stairs, ramps and landings more than 750 mm above grade must be at least how high?
n: Sec. A.5.4: protective railings are at least 1100 mm high where the floor is more than 750 mm above adjacent grade, in addition to the 700 and 900 mm handrails.

q: Where should signage for roadworks on a carriageway be located?
o: At the center of the road
n: Roadwork signage on the carriageway is placed at verges or similar locations.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, ramps longer than 10.50 m need intermediate landings of what minimum length?
n: Sec. A.1.2(d): ramps longer than 10.50 m get intermediate landings at least 1800 mm long (the 1994 IRR required 1.50 m).

q: What judicial role may an architect exercise between a client and a contractor?
o: A function limited to fee collection
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: The architect may exercise judicial functions between client and contractor and must act with entire impartiality.

q: When is railing required at a ramp edge?
o: When the gradient is flatter than 1:20
When the rise exceeds 0.20 m to vehicular traffic
When the ramp is longer than 3.00 m
n: Railing is required when the rise exceeds 0.20 m to vehicular traffic.

q: What is the specified width of a curb cut-out?
n: A curb cut-out is specified at 0.90 m wide.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how far may grating members project above or be recessed below a walkway?
n: Sec. B.3.5: gratings along walkways may not project or be recessed more than 6 mm, with clear spacing of at most 13 mm (the 1994 IRR allowed 6.5 mm).

q: How should routes intended to guide a blind person generally be configured?
n: The recommended route is straightforward with right-angle turns.

q: What is BP 344 commonly known as?
n: BP 344 is identified as the Accessibility Law, which requires accessibility facilities and devices for disabled persons.

q: How should tactile blocks or surfaces be designed relative to shoe soles and wheelchairs?
o: High enough to trip wheelchairs for warning
High enough to be felt by shoe soles but low enough not to cause tripping or hinder wheelchairs
n: The tactile surface must be perceptible underfoot without creating a tripping hazard or obstructing wheelchairs.

q: How many accessible seats are required in a jeepney?
n: Two accessible seats are required in a jeepney, preferably the front seats.

q: What kickboard height is specified for excavation covers?
n: A 0.20 m kickboard is specified with the 1.20 m excavation cover.

q: What should distinguish accessibility signage for easier detection and reading?
o: Contrasting colors and contrasting graphic markers
n: Contrasting colors and graphics help signs be detected and read easily.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what minimum imprisonment applies to abuse of the privileges granted to persons with disabilities?
n: Abuse of privileges: imprisonment of not less than 6 months, or a fine of Php 5,000 to Php 50,000, or both.

q: What should an accessible crossing do relative to the nearest normal pedestrian desire line?
o: Be nearest to or contiguous with the normal pedestrian desire line
Cross only at the road midpoint
n: The crossing should be nearest to, or contiguous with, the normal pedestrian desire line.

q: Where should the accessible seats on a regular bus be located?
o: Near the exit or entrance doors
n: The accessible seats are positioned near the exit or entrance doors for easier access.

q: What is the required top-of-rail height for fencing around roadworks and footworks?
n: The top of the rail is 1.00 m above the adjacent surface.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how should accessible parking slots be oriented?
o: Perpendicular to or at an angle to the road or circulation
n: Sec. A.6.6: wherever possible, accessible slots are perpendicular or at an angle to the road or circulation aisles.

q: What surface material is required for accessible walkways and passageways?
n: Accessible walkways and passageways use a slip-resistant material.

q: Where should flashing emergency-exit lights or signs be placed?
n: Flashing lights or signs are required at every change of direction.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what fine applies to abuse of the privileges granted to persons with disabilities?
n: Abuse of privileges: a fine of Php 5,000 to Php 50,000, or imprisonment of not less than 6 months, or both.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum width of sidewalks, walkways and pathways?
n: Sec. B.3.4: sidewalks and walkways are at least 1500 mm wide, or 1800 mm where two wheelchairs must pass (the 1994 IRR required 1.20 m).

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what imprisonment range applies to a first violation?
n: First violation: a fine of Php 50,000 to Php 100,000, or 6 months to 2 years of imprisonment, or both, at the court's discretion.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, one accessible female and one accessible male toilet cubicle are required on each floor for every how many gendered cubicles?
n: Sec. C.6.2: each accessible floor has at least one accessible female and one accessible male cubicle for every 20 or fewer gendered cubicles.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum clear corridor width?
n: Sec. C.5.1: corridors are at least 1500 mm wide so a wheelchair user and a walking person can pass (the 1994 IRR required 1.20 m).

q: When acting as a professional adviser to a client, what quality must characterize the architect's advice?
o: It must follow the client's preferred opinion
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: The architect acts as a professional adviser and the advice must be unprejudiced.

q: In BP 344's original (1994) anthropometric data, what is the length range of a wheelchair?
n: The anthropometric data gives a wheelchair length of 1.10 to 1.30 m. The 2024 Revised IRR does not restate these body measurements; its turning spaces are 1.80 m × 1.80 m.

q: What is the preferred central refuge width for a 10.00 m carriageway?
n: The preferred central refuge width is 2.00 m.

q: In BP 344's original (1994) anthropometric data, what comfortable reach range is given for a person in a wheelchair?
n: Comfortable reach in a wheelchair is stated as 0.70 to 1.20 m. The 2024 Revised IRR does not restate these body measurements; its turning spaces are 1.80 m × 1.80 m.

q: What proportion of public telephone units must be accessible?
n: One in every four public telephone units (1/4) is made accessible to persons with disabilities.

q: Who is the intended user group for vibra-alarms?
n: Vibra-alarms are intended for deaf or hearing-impaired occupants.

q: What handrail height is specified above steps or ramps?
n: Handrail height above steps or ramps is 0.70 m.

q: What minimum headroom is specified for walkways?
n: Accessible walkways require 2.0 m minimum headroom, preferably higher.

q: What surface should accessible stair treads have?
n: Stair tread surfaces should be slip-resistant.

q: Which official is associated with NHCP?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Maria Serena I. Diokno is identified as the NHCP official.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, a floor has 30 female toilet cubicles. How many of them must be accessible?
n: Sec. C.6.2: one accessible cubicle is needed for every 20 or fewer, so 30 cubicles need 2.

q: Where should audio-visual alarms be provided?
o: In all fire sections as per PD 1185
n: Audio-visual alarms are provided in all fire sections in accordance with PD 1185.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, who is held liable when the violator is a corporation, organization or similar entity?
n: When the violator is a corporation, organization or similar entity, its officials are the ones held liable under RA 7277 Sec. 46 (as amended by RA 9442).

q: What slope/gradient is specified for walkways and passageways?
n: The specified walkway slope is 1:20, equivalent to 5%.

q: Which restroom symbols are identified for men and women?
o: Square for men; circle for women
Circle for men; triangle for women
Triangle for men; circle for women
n: The signage identifies a triangle for men's washroom and a circle for women's washroom.

q: What turnaround dimension is required at every dead end?
n: A 3.50 m turnaround is required at every dead end.

q: Which arrangement is identified as the most beneficial form of crossing?
o: Light-controlled crossing with pedestrian phases and synchronized audible signals
n: The most beneficial form uses light control, pedestrian phases, and synchronized audible signals.

q: Which government officials are jointly assigned responsibility for administration and enforcement?
o: Secretary of Public Works and Highways and Secretary of Transportation and Communication
n: The responsibility is assigned to the Secretary of Public Works and Highways together with the Secretary of Transportation and Communication.

q: Which official is associated with MMDA?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Francisco N. Tolentino is identified as the MMDA official.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what height range is set for the elongated lip of an accessible urinal?
n: Sec. C.6.12: wall-hung urinals have an elongated lip 350 to 400 mm above the floor, with a 900 × 900 mm clear space in front (the 1994 IRR gave 0.48 m).

q: Where else may a dropped curb be provided besides a pedestrian crossing?
o: At the end of a private street or access-road walkway
n: The rule also identifies the end of walkways of a private street or access road.

q: What feature is used to address a change in level at a pedestrian crossing?
n: A dropped curb is used to handle a change in level at pedestrian crossings and similar access points.

q: What is the maximum height for accessible lavatories?
n: The lavatory height is limited to 0.80 m maximum.

q: Where should accessibility signage be located?
o: At a point conveniently seen by a person with disability
n: Signs should be placed where they can be conveniently seen by persons with disabilities.

q: At what height should the water-closet flush control be located?
n: The flush control is located at 1.20 m high.

q: What is the maximum distance of an elevator from an entrance?
n: The elevator location is limited to 30.00 m maximum from the entrance.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum opening force for an interior door closer?
n: Sec. C.2.4: interior door closers may not need more than 2.0 kg of opening force (the 1994 IRR gave 1.0 kg for interior doors).

q: Who may be liable for a violation involving a building, establishment, or structure?
o: Owner/operator, contractor, architect, engineer, and responsible building official
n: The liable persons include the owner or operator, contractor, architect, engineer, and the public official responsible for the permit, registration, certification, or inspection.

q: What curb height is specified at ramps?
n: Ramp curbs are specified at 0.10 m on both sides.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what maximum cross gradient toward the road must a dropped sidewalk have?
n: Sec. B.1.5: dropped sidewalks slope toward the road at a cross gradient of at most 1:100 (1%) so water does not collect (the 1994 IRR gave 1:20).

q: How many accessible seats are required in a passenger train car?
n: A passenger train provides 6 accessible seats per car.

q: What clear walkway width is required between the front ends of accessible parking cars?
n: The walkway between the front ends of cars is 1.20 m.

q: What responsibility does an architect have toward professional associates and subordinates?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: The professional statement expressly recognizes moral responsibilities toward professional associates and subordinates.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear headroom is required where a sign projects over a walkway?
n: Sec. A.7.5: signs projecting into a walkway leave at least 2200 mm of headroom (the 1994 IRR required 2.00 m).

q: Which combination is said to be necessary for an architect's duties and responsibilities to be properly discharged?
o: Motives, conduct, moral values, and ability that command respect and confidence
Legal knowledge and construction speed only
Technical skill and financial success alone
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Professional Ethics
n: The stated professional standard requires motives, conduct, moral values, and ability sufficient to command respect and confidence.

q: Where should the accessible seats on a first-class or air-conditioned bus be located?
o: At the center of the bus
n: The designated seats are placed near the door.

q: Which official is associated with DPWH?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Rogelio Singson is identified as the DPWH official.

q: What handrail height is specified on straight paths?
n: The height for straight paths is 0.90 m.

q: How far should a handrail extend beyond the start or end of ramps or stairs?
n: The handrail extension is 0.30 m at the start and end of ramps or stairs.

q: What length range is specified for kick plates?
n: Kick plates are specified from 0.30 to 0.40 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the steepest gradient allowed for a curb ramp?
n: Sec. B.2.3: curb ramps may not be steeper than 1:15 (the 1994 IRR allowed 1:12). They are only allowed on sidewalks wider than 3300 mm; otherwise dropped sidewalks are used.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what turning space must be provided outside accessible water-closet cubicles?
n: Sec. C.6.3(i): a turning space of at least 1800 × 1800 mm is provided outside the cubicles (the 1994 IRR gave 2.25 m with a 1.50 m minimum).

q: What vestibule dimensions are specified?
n: The specified vestibule size is 1.80 m deep by 1.50 m wide.

q: Which location is specifically associated with dropped curbs?
n: Dropped curbs are provided at pedestrian crossings and at the ends of walkways of private streets or access roads.

q: What diameter and depth are specified for elevator button controls?
n: Buttons are specified at 20 mm diameter and 1 mm depth, with Braille-type signs.

q: Which principle is concerned with enabling disabled citizens to participate and contribute to development goals?
n: Workability and efficiency require the environment to allow disabled citizens to participate and contribute to development goals.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height, on center, is the accessible elevator car operating panel installed?
n: Sec. C.8.7(a): the accessible car operating panel is installed 900 mm on center from the floor; Braille floor indicators go on the door jambs at 1200 mm.

q: Which official is associated with HUDCC?
ref: Professional Practice Tables, p. 72 — Government Officials
n: Jejomar C. Binay is identified as the HUDCC official.

q: What knee and leg clearance is given under tables?
n: The required knee and leg space under tables is 0.70 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what share of the total seating in auditoriums, arenas and theaters must be wheelchair spaces?
n: Sec. E.4.1: 3% of total seating capacity is set aside as wheelchair spaces. This replaces the 1994 table of 2, 4 and 6 seats by capacity.

q: Who is listed as liable for violations involving air, land, and sea transportation?
o: Owner/operator, body builders, safety officers/engineers/managers, drivers/conductors, and responsible public official
n: For air, land and sea transportation, liability extends to the owner/operator, body builders, safety officers, engineers and managers, drivers and conductors, and the public official in charge of permits, registration and inspection.

q: Which principle aims to reduce hazards to life and death while moving through the environment?
n: Safety means designing so people can move with fewer hazards to life and death.

q: What is the maximum length given for a busy or lengthy walkway space before another provision is needed?
n: The maximum length is stated as 12.00 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum difference in level between the base of a dropped sidewalk and the road or gutter?
n: Sec. B.1.6: the base of a dropped sidewalk may sit no more than 19 mm above the road or gutter (the 1994 IRR allowed 25 mm).

q: What is the minimum clear width of an accessible ramp?
n: The minimum clear ramp width is 1.20 m.

q: How should stair nosings be treated?
n: Nosings should be slip-resistant and slanted, with open stringers avoided.

q: Where should the emergency-exit sign plan be located?
n: The emergency-exit tablets or plan are located at the main lobby.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height range are manual switches installed?
n: Sec. C.4.1: manual switches are 900 to 1200 mm above the floor, measured to the center of the switch plate.

q: What is the main purpose stated in BP 344's title?
o: To require certain buildings, institutions, establishments, and public utilities to install accessibility facilities and devices
To establish the National Building Code
n: BP 344 seeks to enhance the mobility of disabled persons by requiring accessibility facilities and devices in specified buildings, institutions, establishments, and public utilities.

q: In BP 344's original (1994) anthropometric data, what clear distance is kept from room corners for wheelchair use?
n: A 0.40 m distance from room corners is provided in the anthropometric data. The 2024 Revised IRR does not restate these body measurements; its turning spaces are 1.80 m × 1.80 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what diameter must full-grip handrails and grab bars have?
n: Sec. A.5.6: full-grip handrails and grab bars have a round section 30 to 40 mm in diameter (the 1994 IRR allowed up to 50 mm).

q: How many accessible seats should be provided on a passenger aircraft, and where?
o: 2 seats near the front exit/entrance door
n: Passenger airplanes provide 2 accessible seats near the front exit or entrance door.

q: If a footway is reduced to less than 1.20 m, how wide must the excavation cover be?
o: The full width of the footway
n: When the footway becomes narrower than 1.20 m, the cover must extend across the full width of the footway.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum footprint of a single wheelchair seating space in an assembly area?
n: Sec. E.4.5: each wheelchair space is at least 900 × 1200 mm, clear, firm and level.

q: Where should accessible parking NOT be located?
n: Accessible parking should not be placed at ramped or sloping areas.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what imprisonment range applies to subsequent violations?
n: Subsequent violations: a fine of Php 100,000 to Php 200,000, or 2 to 6 years of imprisonment, or both.

q: What speed is used to calculate the flashing green period?
n: The flashing green period is based on 0.90 m/sec, not 1.20 m/sec.

q: After arrival, how long is the stated disembarkation period for domestic shipping?
n: The stated disembarkation period after arrival is 1 hour.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum length of a ramp built at 1:15?
n: Table A.1.1: a 1:15 ramp may run up to 10.50 m (a rise of 700 mm), with landings every 10 m; a 1:20 ramp needs landings every 15 m. The 1994 IRR allowed 6.00 m runs at 1:12.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what fine range applies to a first violation?
n: First violation: a fine of Php 50,000 to Php 100,000, or 6 months to 2 years of imprisonment, or both. BP 344 relies on this Magna Carta penal clause.

q: For a 10.00 m carriageway, what minimum central refuge width is given?
n: For a 10.00 m carriageway, the central refuge should be at least 1.50 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height are vertical door pulls centered?
n: Sec. C.2.12: vertical door pulls, preferred on swing doors, are centered 900 mm above the floor (the 1994 IRR gave 1.06 m).

q: What cross gradient is specified for accessible walkways?
n: The cross gradient is 1:100.

q: At what heights should the two ramp handrails be installed?
n: Ramp handrails are provided on both sides at 0.70 m and 0.90 m.

q: How thick should raised symbols, letters, and numbers be?
n: Raised symbols, letters, and numbers are specified at 1 mm, with Braille symbols included.

q: What railing dimension is specified across the full width at the lower end?
n: The railing is 1.80 m across the full width at the lower end.

q: Under RA 7277 (Magna Carta for Disabled Persons) Sec. 46, as amended by RA 9442, what fine range applies to subsequent violations?
n: Subsequent violations: a fine of Php 100,000 to Php 200,000, or 2 to 6 years of imprisonment, or both.

q: Where are dropped curbs and cut-outs provided for accessible parking?
n: Dropped curbs and cut-outs are provided at raised walkways.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what height are handrails provided at the front and sides of accessible assembly seating?
n: Sec. E.4.7: accessible seating in assembly areas has handrails 750 mm high at the front and sides.

q: When does the accessible-unit computation require a minimum of one accessible unit?
o: When the total is divisible by 2
n: The rule states that at least one accessible unit must be provided in all cases.

q: What is the purpose of pavement markings and signs in accessible parking?
o: To delineate parking spaces for persons with disabilities
n: Pavement markings and signs identify the spaces reserved for persons with disabilities.

q: Where should accessible seats in a jeepney preferably be located?
n: The two accessible seats are preferably the front seats.

q: What clearance is required from ledges?
n: The stated clearance from ledges is 40 mm.

q: When are curb cut-outs permitted?
o: Only when the curb is 1.20 m high
When they do not obstruct a walkway or lessen its width
Only where the roadway is sloped
n: Curb cut-outs are allowed only when they do not obstruct a walkway or reduce its width.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, for crossings and walkways narrower than 1500 mm, how deep must the level area at the bottom of a dropped sidewalk be?
n: Sec. B.1.3: where the crossing or walkway is under 1500 mm wide, the level base at the bottom of the dropped sidewalk is at least 1500 mm deep.

q: How many entrance levels should provide elevator access?
n: Elevator access is provided at one entrance level.

q: How should open-space edges be defined to guide blind users?
o: With planters, dwarf walls, a grass verge, or similar textured treatment
n: Open-space edges can be defined by planters with dwarf walls, grass verges, or similar texture-changing features.

q: Where should the accessible entrance be located?
o: At lobby arrival and departure points
n: Entrances are located at lobby arrival and departure points.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the maximum height of a threshold or sliding-door track?
n: Sec. C.3.1: thresholds and door tracks are at most 12 mm high and bevelled above 6 mm (the 1994 IRR allowed 25 mm).

q: What minimum cover width is specified for excavations?
n: Excavation covers are 1.20 m wide with a 0.20 m kickboard.

q: In BP 344's original (1994) anthropometric data, what turning diameter is used for a wheelchair?
n: The stated wheelchair turning diameter is 1.50 m. The 2024 Revised IRR does not restate these body measurements; its turning spaces are 1.80 m × 1.80 m.

q: What material should be used at the leading edge of stairs?
o: Non-skid material with a high-contrast color
n: The leading edge should use non-skid material in a high-contrast color.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how far from the latch side of a door are manual switches placed?
n: Sec. C.4.2: manual switches are 200 mm on center from the latch side of the door.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what walking speed is used to set the steady green period for pedestrians with disabilities?
n: Sec. B.5.8: crossing times for persons with disabilities are based on a walking speed of 0.90 m/sec instead of the usual 1.20 m/sec.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what turnabout space is provided in corridors, spaced at most 12.00 m apart?
n: Sec. C.5.2: turnabout spaces are at least 1800 × 1800 mm, at most 12.00 m apart, and within 3.50 m of every dead end (the 1994 IRR used 1.50 × 1.50 m).

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, at what maximum height, to the center of the sign, is graphic, text and Braille signage installed on walls and doors?
n: Sec. A.7.6: graphic, text and Braille signs on walls and doors are mounted no higher than 1500 mm to the center of the sign.

q: Which principle states that all persons, disabled or not, should be able to use and enjoy the environment?
n: Usability means the built environment should be usable and enjoyable by persons whether disabled or not.

q: A first-class or air-conditioned bus has a 40-person capacity. How many accessible seats are required?
n: A 40-person first-class or air-conditioned bus requires 4 accessible seats near the door.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what maximum opening force is set for exterior hinged doors?
n: Sec. C.2.5: wind, gaskets and door weight make exterior doors vary, so no maximum opening force is set; automatic doors are preferred. Interior doors are capped at 2.0 kg.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what size is door-mounted signage for accessible toilets and showers?
n: Sec. A.7.7: door-mounted signage for accessible toilets and showers is 200 × 200 mm, the minimum for any wall or door sign.

q: Which accessibility principle requires the built environment to avoid criteria that hinder use by disabled or non-disabled persons?
n: Accessibility requires the built environment to be usable by all people without criteria that impede access.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what is the minimum width of an accessible parking slot?
n: Sec. A.6.7: accessible parking slots are at least 4000 mm wide and 5000 mm long; the extra width leaves room for a wheelchair beside the car (the 1994 IRR required 3.70 m).

q: Where should the accessible train seats be positioned?
o: At the rear of the car
n: The 6 accessible seats per car are located nearest the door.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what gradient should accessible ramps not exceed?
n: Sec. A.1.2(b): ramps should be no steeper than 1:20; 1:15 is allowed in special cases, for a length of up to 10.50 m (the 1994 IRR allowed 1:12).

q: What depth is specified for the knee recess under lavatories?
n: The knee recess depth is 0.50 m.
